title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
author: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Logesh L, Aliyas Ahmad Misri
description: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. summary: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget.
takeaways: Everything is simulated on two small models with the simplest quantizer; a title-level search found no earlier study of quantization together with option order.
Averaging four cyclic orders recovers +12.6 points at 4 bits for 0.6B (+5.3 at fp16).

In cost-matched pairs, extra orders beat extra bits only when the weights have 6 or more bits, and the decision table reduces to: use 6-bit weights and spend the rest of the budget on up to four orders, one pass each.
